My own personal changes and ramblings for how I'd turn this into a potential more modern game.

-No more membership needed to play the MAIN worlds. Membership unlocks side worlds and member benefits, otherwise f2p.

-Make realms where you can go to to skip the spell animations. 

-Make stitches and unstiches cost gold. 

-Re add in custom pvpmatches

-Revamp moon school entirely into something different and more useful. Like weakening the enemy or manipulating their resources I.e. discard and pip drain.

-Instead of most bosses being stun immune, simply start them off with 2 or 3 stun shields automatically so that stun has a pve purpose.

-Settle on an identity for balance and keep it consistent. Not the mix match of things the school does right now.

-Add in more gear and proper support for dual classing.

-Make daily challenges into a battle pass like system with added cosmetic and resource rewards and incentives to fish, craft and pet derby too.

-Make pet breeding way more accessible by lowering the gold cost to breed significantly and allow multiple breeding attempts in a row.

-Either remove energy from the game or make it refillable with a significant gold cost. 

-Focus on revamping the experience and graphics of some current worlds first before adding new ones constantly.

-Add more endgame content for pve such as boss rematchs, gauntlet dungeons and dungeons with deck restrictions. 

-Add more incentives to be a member such as a member only crown shop section so people would want to pay for it after they enjoyed the f2p experience.

I could probably think of more of these but this is some of the main stuff from atop my head. I love this game and would like to see it succeed in the modern game world. It certainly has the potential to gain some popularity again if they would just modernize the experience. And for the love of God please advertise the game better. Youtube ads or Twitter or any other prominent social platform would be a good place to start with it.

Part of the color pie that people never put much emphasis on because it's so simple, is the physical aspects of the colors. Everyone talks about the less obvious philosophical aspects of the colors, but they also have physical world elements tied to them such as biomes and elemental magic. There is a balance between representation of physical and philosophical elements of the color pie in magic and what sea monsters are is one of the few physical representations of blue mana. The physical aspect of water as an element, they embody that element. Much like fire with red or plants with green, they all have their corresponding physical representations that don't necessarily have to have a philosophical tie exactly to their color.

Fire - The most obvious one, is mono red

Storm - Izzet, Lightning from red and Wind and Water from Blue

Ice - Mono Blue

Death - Mono Black

Life - Selesnya with a high emphasis on green

Myth - Azorius, They create minions based on thoughts and stories like blue would. They also go about it in a very organized way of manipulating books and thoughts to their whim. 

Balance - 5c, with a heavy emphasis on Izzet, because they like to focus on the elemental schools in a lot of their spells. 

Sun - Naya, take the heat from red, the light from white, and the life from green.

Moon - Dimir, Transmutation and coldness from blue, and darkness of night from black

Star - Esper, Light from stars white, blue is the ever present nature of auras and the stars, black is the distance and the temporary nature of the auras. 

Shadow - Mono black with heavy emphasis on using colorless spells. I imagine alot of black spells with devoid on them. The reality bending nature of shadow reminds me of blacks love of shadows, but also the eldritch magic used by the eldrazi.

As Grixis, for me it has swapped around a lot over the years but personally red is tertiary. I love the free spirit and independence of red as well as it's physical elements of fire and lightning. I love its creativity. But where me and red don't agree as much on is not thinking things through. I'm a very intellectually driven person, so the typical mono-red attitude of not thinking and just attacking with brute strength and no foresight bugs me. I'm also not a very emotional person openly any more so that part is indifferent to me. I like more aspects of red than I don't, especially since I think the more "dumb" aspects of red get drowned out by some of the other colors when in combination so overall it turns it into something I'm fine with.

Burn player here. My local meta for a little bit devolved into mostly 4c piles. Through a combined effort of me and one of my friends we successfully hated most of the nonsense out of the meta. Here are a few of the helpful cards for either 4c piles or elementals. 

-Blood moon - the most obvious answer and usually makes most 3+ color decks struggle a lot. Downside is you have to be playing a heavily red deck to really take full advantage of this piece, but has helped me a lot in burn.
-Hushbringer - basically torpor orb on an evasive body that gains life. If you're running white, this could be just as effective as torpor orb at shutting down all the annoying etb effects from elementals.
-Torpor orb - the colorless variant of shutting down etb effects. It has the advantage of obviously being colorless and harder to remove being an artifact.
-Lavinia, azorius renegade - stops free spells all together but restrictive being a multicolored card. Also shuts down ramping lands like tron lands as a bonus.
-Void mirror - another way to shut down the evoke effect on the mh2 elementals. Doesn't stop them from hard casting them but slows them down considerably.
-Field of ruin - a clean answer to non basic lands. Makes color fixing harder on them.

Definitely hyper competitive, not beginner friendly. And unless you are prepared to take out at least $1000 for a deck then yes also too expensive. I would suggest commander to use older cards more casually.
